Sure! Below are a couple of quick ways you can post that comment to VirusTotal.  
Just replace `ABC321` with your real API key (keep it secret) and run the command or script.

---

## 1️⃣  **cURL (command‑line)**

```bash
curl -X POST "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments" \
     -H "x-apikey: ABC321" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{
           "type": "comment",
           "attributes": {
             "text": "Confirmed #malware"
           }
         }'
```

*If you’re on Windows PowerShell, wrap the JSON in single quotes (`'…'`) or escape the double quotes.*

---

## 2️⃣  **Python (requests library)**

```python
import requests
import json

API_KEY = "ABC321"
IP = "192.168.1.1"

url = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/{IP}/comments"
headers = {
    "x-apikey": API_KEY,
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
}
payload = {
    "type": "comment",
    "attributes": {
        "text": "Confirmed #malware"
    }
}

response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, data=json.dumps(payload))

print("Status:", response.status_code)
print("Response:", response.json())
```

> **Tip:**  
> *If you don’t have `requests` installed, run `pip install requests` first.*

---

### Things to keep in mind

| ✅ | Note |
|---|------|
| 1 | **Private IPs** – 192.168.x.x is a private network address. VirusTotal may not accept comments for private IPs; you’ll get a 404 or 400 error. |
| 2 | **Rate limits** – The free tier allows 4 requests/minute. If you hit the limit, you’ll see a `429 Too Many Requests`. |
| 3 | **API key safety** – Never expose your key in public repos or shared scripts. Use environment variables or a secrets manager. |
